full_judgment:
10. The appellate Court on consideration of the deposition of the plaintiffs' witnesses disbelieved the possession of the plaintiffs observing that the witnesses could not state the plot and khatian numbers and that the defendant No.2 being an admitted co-sharer by inheritance in the suit land, has sold the land in favour of the defendant No.1 by registered sale deed dated 17.03.1993 and thereby the defendant No.2, and for that matter after the purchase, the defendant No.1 is in possession of the suit land and therefore no permanent injunction can be allowed. Therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court was set aside. Being aggrieved there-against plaintiffs as petitioners moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3906 of 1997, the Rule issued therein was heard and disposed of by a Single Bench of the High Court Division vide judgment and order dated 31.10.2007 making the Rule absolute and setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below and restored the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bishwanath, Sylhet, in Title Suit No.54 of 1993, allowing the permanent injunction. 

 "Learned Additional District Judge held that none of 3 P.Ws could mention khatian and plot number of the suit land while they were cross-examined by the learned defence counsel. But this finding has no merit at all since it is admitted that the plaintiffs had title thereto. Learned Additional District Judge placed reliance upon the evidence of 3 defence witness. D.W.1 Anowar Hossain was the Attorney of defendant No.1 Azam Khan, purchaser of the suit land from the defendant No.2 he was the brother-in-law of defendant No. 1. The said D.W. 1 could not also state the boundary and plot number of the suit land when cross examined by the learned advocate for the plaintiffs. D.W.2 Mosoddor was also related to D.W. 1 Anowar Hossain and defendant No.1 Azam Khan. He stated that he was the paternal uncle of Azam Khan (defendant No.1) 

 He also stated in his cross-examination that he could not state the boundary and plot number of the suit land. If the learned Additional District Judge disbelieved plaintiffs possession in the suit land only because of the said 3 P.Ws having failed to state in their cross-examination the plot and khatian number of the suit land, fail to understand how he believed in defendant No. 1's possession in the suit land when D.W.1 and D.W.2 failed to Mention the boundary and plot number of the suit land. Moreover D.W.1 Anwor Hossain and D.W.2 Masaddar Khan were also closely related with defendant No. 1. D.W.3 was the scribe of the kabala whereby defendant No.2 transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant No.1. He was not a witness of possession. 

 13. We have perused the leave petition and the judgment of the High Court Division as well as those of the courts below. Admittedly the suit property belonged to Nosibullah and after his death the said land was inherited by the plaintiff Nos. l and 2, being son and daughter, and by defendant No. 2, being son of the predeceased daughter Korfulennessa, and that as per law of inheritance in the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and defendant No.2 are co-sharers to the extent of their respective shares and that plaintiffs were in physical possession of the suit land and that the suit land not being partitioned the said plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and defendant No.2 were in ejmali possession, though the defendant No.2 was not in physical possession, and that the defendant No.2 being a co-sharer has sold out his share to the defendant No.1 in the suit land, thereby the defendant No.1, subject to validity of his purchase, became a co-sharer in the suit land and he may pursue his claim for possession through a partition suit, if so advised. We have also perused the deposition of the P.Ws and D.Ws, copy annexed to the leave petition, and observe that the P.Ws. stated about possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land but could not state the plot numbers whereas the D.W.2 in his cross-examination has stated that “আব্দুল বসির ৩ বৎসর পূর্বে শ্রীধরপুর চলিয়া যায়। নালিশী বাড়ী হইতে সোয়া মাইল দূরে হইবে।” which goes to show that the defendants could not have any possession on the suit land. The D.W.1 claimed about the possession of the defendant No.1 on the suit land through bargadar but no bargadar was adduced to corroborate the fact of possession of the defendant No.1 and said D.W.1 stated that the village Sridharpur, where the defendant No.2 resides, was about six mile away from the suit land. The D.W.3 was the scribe of the sale deed. He only proved the sale deed and payment of the consideration money. D.Ws.1 and 2 also could not state the plot and khatian numbers of the suit land.
